title: Bug: The “Always On Top” feature does not work with applications running with administrator privileges.
summary: Always On Top reportedly does not work with administrator-elevated applications.

judgment.rationale: The target is reportedly elevated, but PowerToys elevation and behavior on a standard elevated window are unknown.
evidence: On 0.99.1 the reporter says elevated applications including Genshin Impact do not stay on top and Game Mode is off.
Current AlwaysOnTop.cpp warns when its process is not elevated and the foreground window is elevated; that warning does not prove which process ran elevated in the report.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether PowerToys itself ran as administrator and whether a standard elevated application exhibits the same behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: An Always On Top correction may be applicable if the behavior persists with appropriate elevation and a standard target.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate elevated-window pinning
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A privilege mismatch or application-specific topmost behavior may explain the report; neither is established.
plan: Confirm PowerToys and target elevation and reproduce with a standard elevated application.
Compare topmost state and any elevation warning with a non-elevated target and a game where available.
Correct a confirmed supported-case defect while respecting Windows privilege boundaries; do not bypass elevation restrictions.
Add focused regression coverage for the supported process-elevation combinations.
verification: Pinning works in confirmed supported privilege combinations.
Warnings remain appropriate and privilege boundaries are preserved.

confidence.rationale: Process elevation and target-specific behavior are not known.

issue_context.summary: Always On Top reportedly does not work with administrator-elevated applications.
known_information: On 0.99.1 the reporter says elevated applications including Genshin Impact do not stay on top and Game Mode is off.
The reporter did not state whether PowerToys itself was elevated or describe a standard non-game application comparison.
inferences: A privilege mismatch is possible but is not established by the report.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/modules/alwaysontop/AlwaysOnTop/AlwaysOnTop.cpp: on foreground events it checks is_process_elevated and IsProcessOfWindowElevated and may warn about elevation.
Reviewed complete thread and timeline: no comments, assignee, or linked fix. An open-PR title search for Always On Top elevation found no match.
issue_context.analysis: Separate an elevation mismatch from application-specific topmost behavior before proposing a correction.

information_gaps.information: Whether PowerToys was running elevated and whether a standard elevated application also fails.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes process privilege mismatch from game-specific behavior.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reporter checks PowerToys elevation and compares a standard elevated window, following their organization’s security policies.

comment.body:
Thanks for reporting this.

- Was PowerToys itself running as administrator when this occurred?
- Does the same shortcut fail on a standard elevated application (for example, an administrator Command Prompt), or only in the game?

Please follow your organization’s security policies when testing elevation.
